title: Beef Chilli con Carne
description: The most reliable batch meal there is. One pot feeds six and becomes nachos, jacket potatoes and burritos across the week.
ingredients: 800 g canned red kidney beans, drained
steps: Brown the mince hard in the oil, in two batches so it colours rather than steams. Set aside.
Soften the onion and capsicum for 10 minutes, then add the garlic and spices and cook 2 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste, then return the mince with the tomatoes, beans and stock.
Simmer uncovered for 1 hour, until it is thick enough to hold a spoon upright.
Serve with rice.

title: Chicken Enchiladas
description: Rolled, sauced and baked. Assemble a tray on Sunday and it reheats in the oven all week without going soggy.
steps: Poach the chicken in salted water for 15 minutes, then shred it with two forks.
Soften the onion in the oil, add the garlic and spices, then the tomatoes. Simmer 15 minutes and blend smooth.
Mix half the sauce with the chicken and beans.
Roll the filling into the tortillas and pack them seam-side down in a baking dish.
Pour the rest of the sauce over, scatter the cheese, and bake at 190°C for 25 minutes.
Serve with yoghurt and coriander.

title: Pork Carnitas
description: Slow-cooked shredded pork crisped under the grill. Eight serves of a base that becomes tacos, burrito bowls and quesadillas.
ingredients: 2 kg pork shoulder, cut into large chunks
steps: Heat the oven to 160°C. Put everything except the tortillas in a heavy casserole and season heavily.
Cover and cook 3 hours, until the pork falls apart when pushed.
Lift the pork out and shred it. Reduce the cooking liquid on the stove to a syrup.
Spread the pork on a tray, spoon over some of the reduced liquid, and grill on high for 8 minutes until the edges crisp.
Serve in warm tortillas with the remaining juices.

title: Beef Burrito Bowls
description: Built for containers: spiced beef, rice, beans and corn layered so each part keeps its texture.
steps: Start the rice, stirring the lime juice through it once cooked.
Brown the mince in the oil, then add the onion and cook 6 minutes.
Stir in the garlic, spices and tomato paste, then the tomatoes, and simmer 12 minutes.
Fold the beans and corn through and warm for 3 minutes.
Layer rice then beef in bowls or containers.
To store: add the avocado only when you eat, never in advance.

title: Mexican Black Bean Soup
description: Smoky, thick and almost entirely pantry. Cheapest meal on this list and one of the most satisfying.
steps: Soften the onion in the oil for 10 minutes, then add the garlic and spices for 2 minutes.
Add the beans, tomatoes and stock and simmer 20 minutes.
Blend about half the soup and stir it back in — that gives you body without losing all the texture.
Sharpen with lime juice and season well.
Serve with yoghurt and coriander.

title: Chicken Fajita Tray Bake
description: One tray, ten minutes of prep. The capsicum softens by day two but the chicken holds up fine.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C.
Toss the chicken, capsicum and onion with the oil, spices and half the lime juice in one tray.
Roast 30 minutes, turning once, until the edges char.
Squeeze over the rest of the lime.
Serve in warm tortillas with yoghurt and avocado.

title: Mexican Beef Tacos
description: Twenty minutes of spiced mince. Store the filling on its own and it becomes tacos, a salad bowl or a toastie.
steps: Brown the mince hard in the oil.
Add the onion and cook 6 minutes, then the garlic, spices and tomato paste for 2 minutes.
Pour in the stock and simmer 8 minutes until it is saucy rather than wet.
Warm the tortillas.
Build with lettuce, beef, tomato and cheese.

title: BBQ Pulled Pork
description: Five hours in a low oven, ten minutes of work. Freezes in portions and reheats perfectly in its own sauce.
steps: Heat the oven to 150°C. Rub the pork all over with the paprika, sugar, cumin, mustard and plenty of salt.
Sit it on the sliced onion in a deep tray, pour in the stock, and cover tightly with foil.
Roast 4 hours, then uncover and roast 1 hour more.
Shred the pork, discarding any large fat seams.
Reduce the pan juices with the vinegar, tomato sauce and honey to a glossy sauce and toss the pork through.
Pile into rolls with the shredded cabbage.

title: Beef Meatloaf
description: Slices cold straight from the fridge, which makes it a better sandwich the next day than it was a dinner the night before.
steps: Heat the oven to 180°C. Mix both minces with the breadcrumbs, eggs, onion, garlic, mustard, paprika and a lot of salt.
Press into a loaf tin and smooth the top.
Mix the tomato sauce and brown sugar and spread half over the loaf.
Bake 45 minutes, glaze with the rest, and bake a further 15 minutes.
Rest 15 minutes before slicing. Serve with potatoes mashed with the butter.

title: Chicken Pot Pie
description: Creamy chicken and vegetables under puff pastry. Reheat in the oven so the lid crisps up again.
steps: Brown the chicken in half the butter and set aside.
Soften the onion, carrot and celery in the rest of the butter for 10 minutes.
Stir in the flour and cook 2 minutes, then add the stock gradually, stirring, until thick.
Return the chicken with the cream and peas and simmer 10 minutes. Stir in the parsley and season hard.
Tip into a pie dish, lay the pastry over, trim, and brush with egg.
Bake at 200°C for 30 minutes until deeply golden.

title: Beef and Ale Stew
description: The most forgiving thing you can cook. Three hours unattended, six portions, better every day it sits.
ingredients: 1.2 kg beef chuck steak, cut into cubes
steps: Brown the beef in the oil in batches in a heavy pot. Do not crowd the pan.
Soften the onion, carrot and celery for 10 minutes, then add the garlic.
Stir in the flour and tomato paste and cook 2 minutes.
Return the beef with the stock, ale, herbs and plenty of pepper. Simmer covered for 2 hours.
Add the potatoes and simmer uncovered another hour, until the sauce coats a spoon and the beef gives way.
Fish out the bay and rosemary stalks before serving.

title: Baked Mac and Cheese
description: Cheap comfort food that portions into six containers. Reheat with a splash of milk so the sauce loosens again.
steps: Cook the macaroni two minutes short of the packet time and drain.
Melt the butter, whisk in the flour, cook 2 minutes, then add the milk gradually until thick and smooth.
Off the heat, stir in the cheddar, mustard and paprika. Season more than feels right — pasta absorbs it.
Fold the macaroni through and tip into a baking dish.
Top with the breadcrumbs and parmesan and bake at 190°C for 25 minutes.

title: Buffalo Chicken Bowls
description: Hot-sauce chicken with rice and a cooling yoghurt dressing. High protein and genuinely quick.
steps: Start the rice.
Toss the chicken with the oil and paprika, then fry over high heat for 8 minutes until browned and cooked through.
Melt the butter into the hot sauce and toss the chicken through it off the heat.
Mix the yoghurt with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt.
Build bowls with rice, chicken, celery and carrot, and spoon the dressing over. Finish with parsley.

title: Turkey and White Bean Chilli
description: A lighter, paler chilli. Leaner than the beef version and just as good three days later.
steps: Brown the turkey mince in the oil, breaking it up well.
Add the onion and cook 8 minutes, then the garlic and spices for 2 minutes.
Add the beans and stock and simmer 25 minutes, crushing some of the beans to thicken it.
Stir in the corn and lime juice and warm through.
Serve with yoghurt and coriander.

title: Sloppy Joes
description: Sweet-savoury mince in a roll. The filling is a fridge staple — it goes on toast, baked potatoes and pasta too.
steps: Brown the mince in the oil.
Add the onion and capsicum and cook 8 minutes, then the garlic.
Stir in the tomato paste, tomato sauce, sugar, vinegar, mustard and stock.
Simmer 15 minutes until thick and glossy.
Spoon into split rolls.

title: Tuna and Sweetcorn Pasta Bake
description: A pantry bake that costs almost nothing. Six portions from four tins and a packet of pasta.
steps: Cook the pasta two minutes short and drain.
Melt the butter, whisk in the flour, then add the milk gradually until thickened.
Stir in the mustard and two thirds of the cheese, then season well.
Fold through the pasta, tuna, corn and peas and tip into a baking dish.
Top with the remaining cheese and the breadcrumbs and bake at 190°C for 25 minutes.

title: Chicken and Chorizo Paella
description: One wide pan, no stirring. Six serves, and the smoked paprika keeps the leftovers interesting.
steps: Fry the chorizo in the oil in a wide pan until its red fat runs, then set aside.
Brown the chicken in that fat and set aside with the chorizo.
Soften the onion and capsicum for 8 minutes, then add the garlic and paprika.
Stir in the rice for 1 minute, then pour in the stock with the saffron and return the meat.
Simmer without stirring for 20 minutes, then scatter the peas over and cook 5 minutes more.
Rest 5 minutes off the heat. Serve with lemon and parsley.

title: Spanish Albóndigas
description: Pork meatballs in a smoky tomato and almond sauce. Serve with bread and they need nothing else.
steps: Mix both minces with the breadcrumbs, egg, half the garlic and half the paprika. Roll into 24 balls.
Brown them in the oil and set aside.
Soften the onion in the same pan, add the remaining garlic and paprika, then the wine.
Add the tomatoes and ground almonds and simmer 15 minutes — the almonds thicken it.
Return the meatballs and simmer 20 minutes. Finish with parsley.

title: Chorizo and Lentil Stew
description: Smoky, thick and almost free to make. The lentils drink the chorizo fat and it only improves overnight.
steps: Fry the chorizo in the oil until the fat runs red, then lift it out.
Soften the onion and carrot in that fat for 10 minutes, then add the garlic, paprika and tomato paste.
Add the lentils, tomatoes, stock and bay and simmer 30 minutes, until the lentils are soft but not collapsed.
Return the chorizo and season. Finish with parsley.

title: Patatas Bravas Tray Bake with Chorizo
description: Roast potatoes with chorizo and a sharp smoked tomato sauce. Reheat in the oven and the potatoes crisp again.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C. Toss the potatoes with half the oil and roast 35 minutes.
Add the chorizo to the tray and roast a further 10 minutes.
Meanwhile soften the onion in the rest of the oil, add the garlic and paprika, then the tomatoes and vinegar. Simmer 15 minutes and blend smooth.
Spoon the sauce over the potatoes and top with yoghurt and parsley.

title: Spanish Fish and Chickpea Stew
description: Make the tomato and chickpea base ahead; it keeps three days. The fish goes in only when you eat, and lasts one day after that.
ingredients: 600 g white fish fillets, cut into chunks
steps: Soften the onion and capsicum in the oil for 10 minutes, then add the garlic and paprika.
Pour in the wine and let it reduce, then add the tomatoes, stock and chickpeas.
Simmer 15 minutes until thickened.
Slide the fish in, cover, and cook 6 minutes — it is done when it flakes and no longer.
Finish with parsley and serve with lemon.

title: Spanish Tortilla
description: Potato and onion omelette, traditionally eaten at room temperature. Three ingredients and three days of lunches.
steps: Cook the potato and onion gently in the oil in a deep frying pan for 20 minutes, until soft but not browned. Drain, keeping the oil.
Beat the eggs with plenty of salt, then fold the potato and onion through and leave 10 minutes.
Heat 2 tbsp of the reserved oil in the pan and pour the mixture in. Cook on low for 8 minutes.
Slide it onto a plate, invert the pan over it, flip, and cook 5 minutes more.
Cool to room temperature before cutting into wedges.

title: Butter Chicken
description: Mild, rich and universally liked. The sauce protects the chicken through three days of reheating.
steps: Marinate the chicken in the yoghurt with half the spices, ginger and garlic for at least an hour.
Sear the chicken in a hot dry pan until charred at the edges, then set aside — it need not be cooked through.
Melt the butter and soften the onion for 12 minutes, then add the remaining spices, ginger and garlic.
Stir in the tomato paste and tomatoes and simmer 15 minutes, then blend smooth.
Return the chicken with the cream and simmer 10 minutes.
Serve with rice and coriander.

title: Chana Masala
description: Chickpeas in a sharp, spiced tomato sauce. Entirely pantry, meat-free, and one of the cheapest meals here.
steps: Fry the onion in the oil for 12 minutes until properly golden — this is where the flavour comes from.
Add the garlic, ginger and ground spices and cook 2 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and stock and simmer 10 minutes.
Stir in the chickpeas, crush a handful against the side of the pot to thicken, and simmer 15 minutes.
Sharpen with lemon juice. Serve with rice.

title: Lamb Rogan Josh
description: Slow-braised lamb shoulder in a deep red spiced sauce. Two hours, six serves, better on day two.
ingredients: 1.2 kg lamb shoulder, cut into cubes
steps: Brown the lamb in the oil in batches and set aside.
Soften the onion for 12 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger and all the spices and cook 2 minutes.
Take the pan off the heat and stir the yoghurt in a spoonful at a time so it does not split.
Return the lamb with the tomatoes and stock, cover, and simmer 90 minutes.
Uncover and reduce for 20 minutes until the oil rises to the surface. Serve with rice.

title: Dal Tadka
description: Red lentils cooked to a purée and finished with spiced butter. Costs almost nothing and keeps three days.
steps: Rinse the lentils, then simmer with the stock and turmeric for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until collapsed.
Heat the butter and oil in a small pan and fry the onion for 8 minutes until golden.
Add the garlic, ginger, cumin and chilli and fry 1 minute until fragrant, then add the tomato and cook 3 minutes.
Pour this whole spiced butter into the lentils and stir through.
Finish with lemon juice and coriander. Serve with rice.

title: Lamb Koftas with Hummus
description: Spiced lamb skewers with hummus and flatbread. Fast, high protein and good cold in a wrap the next day.
steps: Mix the lamb with the grated onion, garlic, spices and herbs and knead it for a minute — that is what stops the koftas falling apart.
Shape into 12 fat sausages around skewers and chill 15 minutes.
Brush with the oil and grill over high heat for 12 minutes, turning, until charred outside and just pink within.
Warm the pita and spread with hummus.
Top with the koftas, tomato and red onion.

title: Chicken Shawarma Tray Bake
description: Marinated thighs roasted over onions and potatoes. One tray, six serves, and the leftovers make excellent wraps.
steps: Mix the oil, lemon juice, garlic and spices and marinate the chicken for at least an hour.
Heat the oven to 210°C. Spread the potatoes and onions in a large tray and lay the chicken on top so its marinade drips down.
Roast 45 minutes, turning the potatoes once, until the chicken edges blacken.
Slice the chicken and return it to the tray juices.
Serve with yoghurt and parsley.

title: Shakshuka
description: Eggs poached in spiced tomato. Make the sauce in bulk — it keeps three days — and crack fresh eggs into it each time.
steps: Soften the onion and capsicum in the oil for 12 minutes, then add the garlic and spices.
Add the tomatoes and simmer 12 minutes until thick — a watery base means watery eggs.
Make eight wells and crack an egg into each.
Cover and cook 6 minutes, until the whites set and the yolks still move.
Scatter the feta and parsley over and serve with pita.
To store: keep the sauce alone and poach fresh eggs each time.

title: Mujadara
description: Lentils, rice and a mountain of caramelised onion. Meat-free, absurdly cheap, and it keeps for days.
steps: Fry the onions in the oil over medium heat for 25 minutes, stirring often, until deep brown and sweet. Take out half for the top.
Simmer the lentils in the stock for 15 minutes.
Add the rice and spices to the pot with the remaining onion, cover, and cook 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed.
Rest off the heat 10 minutes, then fork through.
Top with the reserved onions, yoghurt and parsley.

title: Baked Fish with Tahini Sauce
description: White fish baked over onions under a lemony tahini sauce. Cooked fish is a one-day proposition, so plan it for a night you are home.
steps: Start the rice. Heat the oven to 200°C.
Soften the onions in the oil for 12 minutes and spread them in a baking dish.
Whisk the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, cumin and water into a pourable sauce. It will seize before it loosens — keep going.
Lay the fish on the onions, season, and pour half the sauce over.
Bake 20 minutes until the fish flakes. Serve with the remaining sauce, parsley and rice.

title: Moroccan Chicken Tagine
description: Chicken with chickpeas, apricots and warm spice. Sweet-savoury, one pot, and it deepens for three days.
steps: Brown the chicken in the oil and set aside.
Soften the onion for 10 minutes, then add the garlic, ginger and spices and cook 2 minutes.
Return the chicken with the tomatoes, stock, chickpeas and apricots.
Simmer uncovered 40 minutes until the sauce thickens and the apricots swell.
Pour boiling stock over the couscous, cover 5 minutes, then fork through.
Serve the tagine over the couscous with coriander.

title: Cajun Sausage and Rice
description: One pot, rice cooked in the pan with everything else. Nothing to drain and nothing to wash up.
steps: Brown the sausage in the oil in a wide pot and set aside.
Soften the onion, capsicum and celery for 8 minutes, then add the garlic and spices.
Stir in the rice for 1 minute, then add the tomatoes and stock and return the sausage.
Cover and simmer 20 minutes without lifting the lid.
Rest 5 minutes off the heat, fork through, and finish with spring onion.

title: Roast Chicken and Vegetables
description: A whole roast chicken is the best value batch cook there is: dinner, then sandwiches, then stock from the carcass.
steps: Heat the oven to 200°C. Push the lemon halves and rosemary into the chicken cavity.
Toss the potatoes, carrots, onion and garlic with the oil and oregano in a large tray and sit the chicken on top.
Pour the stock around the edges and roast 90 minutes, basting once, until the juices from the thigh run clear.
Rest the chicken 15 minutes before carving.
To store: strip all the remaining meat off the bones the same night — it keeps three days, on the carcass it does not.

title: Honey Mustard Salmon Tray Bake
description: Salmon and vegetables on one tray in twenty-five minutes. Cook it for the night you eat it.
ingredients: 600 g potatoes, cut into small cubes
steps: Heat the oven to 210°C. Toss the potatoes with 2 tbsp of the oil and roast 20 minutes.
Mix the honey, mustard, lemon juice, garlic and remaining oil.
Push the potatoes aside, add the broccoli and the salmon, and spoon the glaze over the fish.
Roast a further 12 minutes, until the salmon flakes at the thickest point.

title: Tuscan Tomato and White Bean Soup
description: Thick enough to stand a spoon in, made almost entirely from tins. Ten minutes of work for six lunches.
steps: Soften the onion and carrot in the oil for 10 minutes, then add the garlic, tomato paste and oregano.
Add the tomatoes, stock and beans and simmer 20 minutes.
Blend about a third of the soup and stir it back through for body.
Wilt the spinach in at the end and serve with parmesan.

title: Ginger Pork Noodles
description: Fifteen minutes start to finish. Pork mince, a lot of ginger, and noodles that soak up the sauce.
steps: Cook the noodles and drain.
Brown the pork mince hard in the oil, breaking it up.
Add the ginger and garlic for 30 seconds, then the cabbage and carrot for 3 minutes.
Add the soy sauce, oyster sauce and sugar and toss.
Fold the noodles through, finish with sesame oil and spring onion.

title: Miso Chicken Tray Bake
description: Miso, honey and soy caramelise on the chicken skin as it roasts. Almost no prep and it keeps three days.
ingredients: 600 g sweet potato, cut into wedges
steps: Whisk the miso, honey, soy sauce, sesame oil, ginger and garlic together and coat the chicken.
Heat the oven to 200°C. Toss the sweet potato with the vegetable oil in a large tray.
Lay the chicken on top and roast 40 minutes, turning once, until sticky and dark.
Scatter over the spring onion and sesame seeds.

title: Greek Baked Fish Plaki
description: White fish baked in tomato, onion and oregano. Simple and light, but cooked fish gets one day and no more.
steps: Heat the oven to 190°C. Layer the potato slices in a baking dish with half the oil and season.
Soften the onion in the rest of the oil, add the garlic, then the tomatoes and oregano, and simmer 10 minutes.
Pour half the sauce over the potatoes and bake 25 minutes.
Lay the fish on top, cover with the remaining sauce and the lemon juice, and bake 15 minutes more.
Finish with parsley.
